text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The European Union should be open to all the countries seeking membership, Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said on the first day of his two-day visit to Lithuania.

- Lithuanian politicians are not afraid of threats coming from the Kremlin reiterated their frim desire to seek membership in NATO in the face of Russia's fierce objections. Russia on Tuesday said it might reconsider its new agreement with NATO if it offered the Baltic states membership.
- The current shareholders of Hermis bank used their priority right and acquired 65 percent of the new 23 million litas share issue.
- Lithuania has signed free trade agreement with 24 countries, inlcuding all 15 EU countries.
- The president of Lithuania's soccer federation Vytautas Dirmeikis signed a letter of resignation but declined to say why.
- Lithuania welcomes U.S. State Department statements that the door to NATO membership remains open to the Baltic states.

- The newspaper said that a major stake in the 60 million litas share issue of Litimpeks bank might be acquired by some Norwegian funds and Nomura Securities. Around 10 percent might be offered to Polish Kredyt Bank S.A.
- Lithuania's Agricultural Bank plans to discuss a share capital increase at its June 6 shareholders' meeting.
